# Surveillance Reports {.unnumbered}

## 1. Executive Summary & Purpose

The purpose of this section is to establish a uniform tracking dictionary for monitoring Substance Use Disorders (SUD), acute drug toxicities, chronic alcohol-induced conditions, and critical mental health metrics within our jurisdiction.
Standardizing these metrics allows our epidemiology team to accurately track longitudinal trends, isolate geographic hot-spots, evaluate community-level interventions, and provide actionable evidence to public health leadership.

## 2. Methodological Framework & Origin

The core metrics implemented in this surveillance chapter are derived from the foundational framework established by the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists (CSTE) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
As detailed in the benchmark publication, *"Development of Indicators for Public Health Surveillance of Substance Use and Mental Health"* (Hopkins, Landen, & Toe, 2018), these indicators address a historic public health gap by creating a shared vocabulary for behavioral health tracking.

The workgroup selected these specific metrics using a modified Delphi methodology based on three strict criteria: 1.
**Universal Availability:** Data inputs must be accessible across state and local lines (e.g., Vital Statistics, BRFSS, hospital registries).
2.
**Methodological Validity:** Case definitions must rely on clear, reproducible clinical mapping (such as standardized ICD-9-CM, ICD-10, or ICD-10-CM codes).
3.
**Public Health Actionability:** The data must directly inform policy, resource allocation, or harm reduction strategies.

## 3. Comprehensive Surveillance Indicators Table

cste_full_data |>
gt() |>
tab_header(
title = "CSTE Substance Use & Mental Health Surveillance Framework",
subtitle = "Complete 18-Indicator Matrix (2016 Guidelines)"
) |>
cols_label(
Indicator = "Core Indicator",
Subindicators = "Subindicators / Coding Instructions",
Data_Source = "Data Source",
Age_Group = "Age Profile",
Definition_Brief = "Indicator Definition & Case Logic",
Stratification = "Stratification Variables"
) |>
tab_options(
table.width = pct(100),
heading.title.font.size = px(14),
heading.subtitle.font.size = px(11),
column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
table.font.size = px(10)
) |>
cols_width(
Indicator ~ pct(15),
Subindicators ~ pct(23),
Data_Source ~ pct(12),
Age_Group ~ pct(8),
Definition_Brief ~ pct(28),
Stratification ~ pct(14)
)

::: callout-important
## Privacy and Data Suppression Thresholds

When executing analysis scripts for small geographic divisions (such as zip-code or sub-county cohorts), analysts must apply cell-suppression rules.
If any numerator or case count falls below below ten for hospital discharge ($n < 10$), and for death certificate data ($n < 5$), the cell value must be suppressed to guarantee confidentiality and avoid deductive identification of individuals in administrative datasets.
:::

## 4. Key Data Source Logistics

-   **Vital Statistics (Birth and death certificate):** Serves as the stable denominator for calculating overall population mortality metrics (Indicators 4 and 6). Requires continuous cross-referencing with underlying cause-of-death ICD codes.
-   **Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (SCCHS and YRBS):** Provides self-reported population behavioral data for chronic and acute drinking metrics. Analysts must apply complex survey weights (`_LLCPWT`) when computing prevalence estimates.
-   **Administrative Billing Data (Hospital/ED):** Essential for identifying the near-miss morbidity burden of the illicit drug supply line. Relies on the precision of clinical coding teams at local healthcare facilities.
